questions.q: Per this lesson, why does an organization running Fabric alongside other platforms still need Microsoft Purview's catalog?
options: Because the OneLake catalog is scoped to Fabric — non-Fabric sources like a SQL Server or Snowflake account never show up in it
Because the OneLake catalog has been fully replaced by Purview and no longer functions
Because Purview and the OneLake catalog contain identical information with no difference at all
Because Fabric items cannot be governed at all without Purview
questions.explain: Purview is Microsoft's enterprise-wide catalog, spanning both Fabric and non-Fabric sources — the OneLake catalog only covers the Fabric estate.

questions.q: When should the 'Microsoft Purview MSI (system)' credential be used to scan a Fabric tenant, per this lesson?
options: When Purview and the Fabric tenant sit in the same tenant — it's the simplest option, with no secrets to manage
Only when scanning a completely different, unrelated cloud platform
Never — it is disabled by Microsoft for all Fabric scans
Only when personal workspaces are excluded from the scan
questions.explain: For a same-tenant setup, Purview's own managed identity is the simplest credential choice, requiring no secret management.

questions.q: Why would an organization choose a dedicated service principal over Purview's own managed identity for a scan, per this lesson?
options: For a cross-tenant setup, or when a narrower, more auditable identity than Purview's own MSI is wanted
Because a service principal is required for every single Purview scan, with no exceptions
Because Purview's managed identity cannot be used for any purpose
Because service principals do not require any API permissions
questions.explain: A dedicated service principal fits cross-tenant scenarios or a tighter, auditable identity, as an alternative to Purview's own managed identity.

questions.q: What does granting the registered app's 'Configured permissions' demonstrate, per this lesson?
options: Least privilege — the scanning identity gets exactly the API permissions it needs, granted and auditable
That the app automatically receives full administrator rights across the entire tenant
That API permissions are irrelevant to how a Purview scan actually runs
That the app can never be granted any permissions at all
questions.explain: The permissions pane shows a narrow, deliberately granted set of permissions rather than a standing admin account.

questions.q: What is the difference between the first scan and every scan after it, per this lesson?
options: The first scan is always a full scan; every subsequent scan is incremental
Every scan, including the first, only reads data that changed in the last hour
The first scan is incremental, and only the second scan is ever full
There is no difference — every scan always re-reads everything from scratch
questions.explain: The initial scan captures everything in full; recurring scans after that only track what actually changed.
